entries.clue: Gambling town discovered in venture north (4)

indicators.note: the answer is uncovered sitting inside the following words

annotation.surface: A gambler strikes out northwards and stumbles on a casino town.
annotation.walkthrough: Reno is the Nevada city famous for casinos. The answer spans the gap between the two words, which is why it is easy to read past.
annotation.definitionFit: Reno is a well-known American gambling town.

entries.clue: Can New York make a man? (6)

blocks.note: can and john are both American slang for a toilet

annotation.surface: A question about whether a big city can turn a boy into a man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb opening a question; it is the noun. Johnny is the first half of Johnny Cash, the singer this puzzle is built around.
annotation.definitionFit: A johnny is an informal word for a man or chap.

entries.clue: Aggrieved worker supporting dining out (9)

indicators.note: dining is put out of order
in a down answer, ANT sits underneath and holds up the rest

annotation.surface: A disgruntled employee is stuck propping up customers who are eating out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dining out' reads as a meal in a restaurant; 'out' is the instruction to rearrange. Ant = worker is a crossword staple.
annotation.definitionFit: Indignant means aggrieved, resentful at unfair treatment.

entries.clue: Fair June, dice, cigs, ales - not half! (8)

indicators.note: each word keeps only half of its letters

annotation.surface: A list of vices from a summer fair: gambling, smoking and beer, with an emphatic British 'not half!'
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fair' pretends to be a funfair in June; it is the adjective. 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', here taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: Judicial can mean fair and impartial, as a judge should be.

entries.clue: Vocal expressions complete topless cancans, say (10)

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its top in a down answer
cancans are an example of dances

blocks.note: utter = complete, as in utter nonsense
cancans are DANCES; drop the D

annotation.surface: Something racy: a complete show of topless cancan dancers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' works on DANCES, the word that 'cancans, say' stands for, not on CANCANS itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Utterances are things said aloud, vocal expressions.

entries.clue: Recline - swallow concoction beforehand (3,4)

indicators.note: LIE goes in front of DOWN

blocks.note: a concocted story is a lie
to down a drink is to swallow it

annotation.surface: Advice to take a lie-down after swallowing some potion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concoction' looks like a drink to swallow, but here it is a made-up story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to rest with the body stretched out rather than upright.

entries.clue: Abridge sermon for radio (6)

indicators.note: on the radio it is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a lesson is a reading in church, a kind of sermon

annotation.surface: A producer cuts a preacher's sermon down to fit a radio slot.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'abridge' an instruction about the broadcast; it is the definition, and 'for radio' flags the sound-alike.
annotation.definitionFit: To lessen something is to reduce or cut it down, to abridge it.

entries.clue: Excited outcry about new music sung by 2/7D (7)

indicators.note: the letters of OUTCRY are stirred up
the rearranged letters go round N

annotation.surface: Fans cry out in excitement at a new song from a star.
annotation.walkthrough: 2/7D is JOHNNY CASH, from 2 and 7 down; country is the music he sang.
annotation.definitionFit: Johnny Cash was a country music singer.

entries.clue: American state underpinned by hush money (4)

indicators.note: in a down answer, SH sits beneath CA

blocks.note: CA is the postal code for California

annotation.surface: A US state's affairs are propped up by secret bribes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hush money' looks like one phrase; the clue splits it, with 'hush' in the wordplay and 'money' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, especially for money in notes and coins, and the surname of the singer the puzzle celebrates.

entries.clue: Seen my medley? They always applaud (3-3)

indicators.note: a medley mixes things together

annotation.surface: A performer asks about their medley and notes that the flatterers clap regardless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medley' fits the musical theme of the surface, but here it only means mixed.
annotation.definitionFit: Yes-men agree with and applaud whatever their boss does.

entries.clue: Vowed at first she would only remarry nervously (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

annotation.surface: A widow promises she would only marry again with great hesitation.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about vows in the marriage sense, which keeps 'Vowed' looking like part of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: A past participle for a past participle: to swear an oath is to make a solemn vow.

entries.clue: Fashionable points, retaining rule, making leaders (9)

indicators.note: to retain something is to keep it held within, so SPIRES keeps R inside itself

blocks.note: spires are pointed tops of buildings

annotation.surface: Trendy people who keep their grip on power end up as leaders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Points' suggests compass points (N, S, E, W); it is SPIRES, which take R in before the final S.
annotation.definitionFit: Inspirers are people who inspire others, as leaders do.

entries.clue: In the beginning, Lord working across year (5,2)

indicators.note: EARL and ON stretch across Y, which sits between them

blocks.note: on = working, as a machine is on

annotation.surface: It sounds like Genesis: in the beginning the Lord was busy for a year.
annotation.walkthrough: The biblical opening makes 'Lord' look like God; here it is a peer.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an adverbial phrase for at an early stage, which matches the adverbial 'In the beginning'.

entries.clue: Practising again - listen to squeal (10)

blocks.note: to hear is to listen to
to squeal and to sing are both slang for informing to the police

annotation.surface: A singer going over a piece yet again, with an ear for a squeaky note.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Practising again' looks like the whole definition; 'again' belongs to the wordplay. Squeal and sing share an underworld sense: to inform.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: actors and musicians rehearse by going over a piece to get it right before performing.

entries.clue: Penelope is spinning with mania in hallucination (6)

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the letters are read back to front

blocks.note: Penelope is the setter, so 'Penelope is' = I'M
a rage or mania is a craze

annotation.surface: The setter confesses to spinning in a manic, hallucinatory state.
annotation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves means I or ME; here 'Penelope is' becomes I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical illusion, a kind of hallucination.

entries.clue: Tired editor bolstering talent with hesitation (9)

indicators.note: in a down answer, ED sits under and props up the rest

annotation.surface: An exhausted editor props up a hesitant writer.
annotation.walkthrough: Knackered is British slang for exhausted.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: knackered is informal British for utterly worn out.

entries.clue: 'Lambeth Nick' an enigmatic nickname for singer from the south? (3,3,2,5)

annotation.definition: nickname for singer from the south?

indicators.note: the letters are scrambled into a puzzle

annotation.surface: A London singer called Nick from Lambeth goes by a mysterious nickname.
annotation.walkthrough: Lambeth is a district of south London, which is the 'south' the surface points to; the singer is Johnny Cash, from the American South, known as The Man in Black.
annotation.definitionFit: The Man in Black was Johnny Cash's nickname, from his habit of dressing in black.

entries.clue: Egg on vomit - eat accidentally! (8)

indicators.note: the letters fall into place by accident

annotation.surface: A nasty kitchen mishap: egg lands in sick, which someone then eats by mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Egg' reads as food, fitting the eating surface; 'egg on' is a verb meaning urge.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to spur or urge someone into action.

entries.clue: High notes wobbly over beginning of duet (6)

indicators.note: the letters of NOTES are shaken up
in a down answer, STONE sits above D
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only D is taken from duet

annotation.surface: A singer's high notes waver at the start of a duet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High' reads as pitch; it is the slang for intoxicated.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: both describe someone intoxicated, usually on cannabis.

entries.clue: Cage fighting? RIP then junior (6)

indicators.note: letters that are fighting get knocked about out of their order
then means next in sequence, so SON follows PRI

blocks.note: a son may be a junior, sharing his father's name

annotation.surface: A cage fighter's death is announced, and then his son steps in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cage fighting' looks like one phrase; 'Cage' is the definition and 'fighting' the anagram instruction. Johnny Cash famously played prison concerts.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used loosely: to cage someone is to lock them up, and a cage is a place of confinement.

entries.clue: Warm southern greetings (6)

blocks.note: to toast is to warm, as by a fire

annotation.surface: A friendly welcome in the manner of the South.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as warm Southern hospitality; 'Warm' is a verb in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Toasts are salutes or greetings offered with a raised glass.

entries.clue: Blimey guvnor - sounds like such a fast horse! (7)

indicators.note: the answer is heard in the exclamation

blocks.note: cor = blimey, and guvnor is a respectful sir

annotation.surface: A cockney punter exclaims at how fast a horse is running.
annotation.walkthrough: Cor and blimey are both British exclamations of surprise, and guvnor is a cockney way of addressing a man as sir. The homophone needs a non-rhotic British accent.
annotation.definitionFit: A courser is a swift horse, especially a warhorse or racer.

entries.clue: Buoyant pound following Uruguayan peso to begin with (6)

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so BEAT is placed after UP
each word is used only for what it begins with, its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of Uruguayan and peso

annotation.surface: A market report: sterling rides high against the Uruguayan currency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like sterling in this currency surface; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a cheerful, optimistic mood.

entries.clue: Dressed circa 50 AD (4)

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

annotation.surface: A caption on a Roman costume display: dressed as in about AD 50.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a date; each part of it is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clad is an old past participle of clothe, so it means dressed.

entries.clue: Centre for world class singers - drunken student Elvis? Nah (9)

indicators.note: the letters stagger out of order

annotation.surface: A tipsy student in a music city insists the singer is not Elvis.
annotation.walkthrough: L for student comes from the L-plates on a learner driver's car.
annotation.definitionFit: Nashville, Tennessee, is the centre of country music, home to its star singers.

entries.clue: Low mood music (5)

blocks.note: first sense: a spell of sadness or depression
second sense: the melancholy African-American musical genre

annotation.surface: Melancholy music, the kind that matches a sad mood.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are closely related, which makes the clue read as a single idea.
annotation.definitionFit: Blues means both a low mood and a style of music.

entries.clue: Part of a French sex appeal (4)

blocks.note: it = sex appeal, as in the It girl

annotation.surface: A bit of that French allure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like a hidden-word instruction; 'Part' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a unit is one component of a larger whole, as an army unit is part of the army.

entries.clue: Gifted mafia boss put away diamonds (7)

blocks.note: a mafia boss is a don
to put away food is to eat it

annotation.surface: A mob boss stashes some diamonds, perhaps as a gift.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' suggests hiding the jewels; here it means eaten.
annotation.definitionFit: Donated means gave as a gift, gifted.

entries.clue: Happiness alien to criminal (7)

indicators.note: the letters are treated unlawfully and mangled

annotation.surface: Crooks are strangers to happiness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the subject; it is the anagram instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, pitched stronger: elation is happiness at its most exhilarated.
